# s426 — TUI note delete retracts instead of deleting

In the TUI, saving an item note with an empty body stops deleting the note. It asks for a one-line reason and retracts the note through `ops.retract_note`, the way `slicer note-retract` does, so the text and who, when and why stay on the record.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:** a CLI note-delete command (there is none today); removing `ops.remove_note`, which `test_Legacy_ReadOnlyLift_EditDeletePreserveIdentity` still calls; un-retracting; editing the text of a retracted note (still allowed through `ops.set_note`); legacy slice notes (`slice-legacy-N`), which the TUI does not list as note entries; any change to merge-index note handling.

## Why

s393 added note retraction because "notes are an audit trail": a wrong note is corrected by `retracted_by`, `retracted_at` and `retracted_reason`, never removed (`ops.retract_note` docstring, src/slicer/ops.py:2516-2541). Its boundary left "the TUI's existing edit and delete" as they were, and this row is that follow-up.

Verified against main at 50bd033 on 2026-11-02: the TUI's note entries (`tui.entries`, src/slicer/tui.py:376) open the note in `$EDITOR`. In `apply_edit_result` (tui.py:650-657) an empty body calls `ops.remove_note`, which deletes the record (`del item.note_records[index]`, ops.py:2565-2572) and logs `note` with `note="remove"`. The note's text and its author are gone from the index. `ops.remove_note` has no other production caller (CLI has no note delete). docs/tui.md:22 documents "a note (edit it, or empty to remove ...)". Two tests pin the removal: `test_ApplyEdit_AddEditRemoveNote` (tests/test_tui_style.py:304) and `test_Tui_TypedEditAndDelete_PreserveMetadataAndLabels` (tests/test_note.py:202).

`ops.retract_note(state, item_id, note_id, reason, *, owner)` needs a nonblank one-line reason and refuses an already-retracted note (`usage`). The editor returns only the emptied body, so the TUI needs a second step to collect the reason. The TUI already has a one-line prompt for handoff and reject notes: mode `note` with `note_action` (tui.py:1115-1121, handled in `_note` at tui.py:1388-1416, label at tui.py:1977-1982). This slice adds a `retract` action to it.

Owner question (recommended answer assumed by this spec): collect the reason in that prompt (Enter with an empty reason or Esc cancels and writes nothing). The alternative is to retract at once with a fixed reason such as "removed in the TUI". It needs no prompt, but the record would not say why the note was wrong.

## Files

- `src/slicer/tui.py`:
  - `ActResult` gains `retract: tuple[str, str] | None = None` (item id, note id).
  - `apply_edit_result`, kind `note`, empty body: look up `record = item.note_records[request.index]`. If it is already retracted, return an error `ActResult` ("note already retracted; nothing changed") and write nothing. Otherwise return `ActResult("give a reason to retract the note", retract=(request.target, record.id))` and write nothing yet.
  - `View.accept`: when `result.retract` is set, enter mode `note` with `note_action = "retract"`, empty text, and keep the pair on the view (a new field such as `retract_target`).
  - `_note`: for `retract`, Enter with a blank reason notifies "cancelled". Otherwise call `vcs.require_no_merge(state.root)`, then `ops.retract_note(state, item_id, note_id, reason, owner=None)` (the same actor precedence as `note-retract` without `--owner`), notify "note retracted; press r to render" (`success`) and set `drift_due`. Esc cancels as today. `SlicerError`/`OSError` notify as error.
  - The status-line label for `retract` is "Retract reason, required".
- `tests/test_tui_style.py`, `tests/test_note.py`, `tests/test_tui.py`: the tests below; the two removal tests change to expect retraction.
- `docs/tui.md` line 22: "empty to remove" becomes "empty to retract it: a prompt asks for the reason, and the note stays on the record marked retracted".
- `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` `### Changed`.

## Failing tests

- `test_ApplyEdit_EmptiedNote_AsksForARetractReason` (tests/test_tui_style.py): `apply_edit_result(state, EditRequest("note", "S01", "note 1", text, index=0), "")` returns a result whose `retract` is `("S01", NOTE_ID)`. The index and `log.jsonl` bytes are unchanged and the note is still there, unretracted.
- `test_NoteRetractPrompt_Reason_RetractsAndKeepsText` (tests/test_tui.py, driving the view as the handoff/reject prompt tests near tests/test_tui.py:1310 do): after `view.accept(result)`, typing `wrong item` and Enter leaves the note text unchanged with `retracted_reason` `wrong item`, a nonempty `retracted_by` and `retracted_at`, and one `note-retract` log line naming the note id.
- `test_NoteRetractPrompt_BlankReasonOrEsc_CancelsAndWritesNothing` (tests/test_tui.py): Enter on an empty or whitespace reason, and Esc, leave index and log bytes unchanged and notify "cancelled".
- `test_ApplyEdit_EmptiedRetractedNote_IsErrorAndWritesNothing` (tests/test_tui_style.py): an already-retracted note emptied in the editor returns `severity` `error` and opens no prompt (`retract` is None).
- Update `test_ApplyEdit_AddEditRemoveNote` (rename to `test_ApplyEdit_AddEditRetractNote`) and `test_Tui_TypedEditAndDelete_PreserveMetadataAndLabels` (rename `Delete` to `Retract`): emptying then giving a reason keeps the record, with its kind label, marked retracted, instead of `note_records == []`.
